_comment: Two tabs: the working Overview, and an Integration & Health tab holding sync metrics, the design summary and the runbook. Widgets are independent of the tab they live on.
name: Toronto Events
description: Live view of Toronto events with a map of where they concentrate, plus an Integration & Health tab covering sync metrics, design notes and recovery.

widgets.label: How these counts are defined
widgets.html:
How these counts are defined

  • All day = 00:00–23:59 of that calendar day, in your session timezone.
  • Still to come = from this minute until 23:59 today. It falls to 0 as the day ends, and just after midnight every day card resets — that is the new day, not an outage.
  • Rolling = the next 7 / 30 days counted forward from now, not fixed dates.
  • The six cards ignore the filters above, so they always show true absolute counts. Everything else on this tab — both feeds, the matching list, the charts and the map — does follow them.
  • Some categories are sparse: Dating has 384 events overall but none today and 3 in the next 60 days, so a filtered feed can correctly show 'no data'. Use Matching the filters for an unbounded view of a narrow category.
  • An event whose venue has no coordinates cannot be plotted, so the map shows fewer events than the lists.

Integration at a glance
widgets.html:
Direction  inbound only, one way — feed → ServiceNow. Not bi-directional.

Frequency  designed daily 03:00 America/Toronto; not installed — no timer, no cron entry, no Scheduled Import. Every run to date was manual.

Mechanism  external Python → HTTPS + Basic → Table API, upsert on u_event_id. Not an Import Set, not JDBC; the MID Server is not involved.

Derived each run  u_primary_category and u_location_ref — skip this and new rows drop off the chart and the map.

Timezone  the feed stamps Toronto local time as Z; the import converts to true UTC, DST-aware.

Flow diagram, idempotency mechanics, native-pattern comparison and failure modes are on the Architecture & Data Flow tab.

The MID Server is not in this path. No Import Set, no Transform Map, no JDBC. ServiceNow only ever sees REST calls.

widgets.label: Idempotency
widgets.html:
Idempotency, defined: running the sync twice changes nothing the second time. Six mechanisms enforce that, and each one exists because of a defect that was actually observed.

mechanismhowthe bug it prevents
Natural keymatch on u_event_idduplicate rows on every run
Compare before writevalues_differ() normalises both sides before comparinga PATCH on an unchanged row still bumps sys_updated_on
Numeric tolerancecompare and write at the column precision (lat/lng 6 dp, price 2 dp)float last-digit noise rewrote 15 of 11,940 rows every run
Width preflightabort before writing when a value exceeds the columna 429-char title truncated at 255 re-wrote that row every run, forever
Duplicate collapsecanonicalise_source() keeps the newest u_last_updated per id5 duplicated ids alternated winners each run, a permanent 2-cycle
Format-only DB comparetimezone conversion applies to source values only, never to stored valuesre-syncing after the timezone fix would shift every row another 4–5 hours

Proof, not assertion: two consecutive full syncs produce 0 inserted, 0 updated, 11,940 unchanged. The one-time timezone migration (fix_source_timezone.py) writes a marker file so it cannot run twice by accident.

Deliberately not idempotent: the sweep deletes rows missing from the feed. If the feed is truncated upstream, the sweep mirrors that deletion — use --no-sweep until the feed is trusted.

The native machinery exists here and has never been used: 17 data sources (File 8, OIDC 5, LDAP 2, JDBC 2), 14 transform maps, a JDBC-capable MID (gx10-mid, Up) — and 0 import sets, 0 import-set runs, 0 scheduled imports.

Why scripted: the feed needed work the declarative path does poorly — reinterpreting a bogus Z, width preflight, numeric comparison at storage precision, duplicate collapse, and offline unit tests. The trade-off is real: we re-implemented coalesce and have no import-set history. Move to a File/JSON data source if per-run audit becomes a requirement.

Tracking a scripted table (scripting does not disable update sets)

Capture depends on sys_update_name and scope, not on how a record was created, so REST-created records are captured like any other. Measured here: 960 sys_update_xml rows, 4,066 sys_update_version (30 of them for our sys_dictionary entries), 60,795 sys_audit rows. What scripting costs: capture lands in Default, mixed with everything else (a clean set cannot be opened over REST — select it in the UI first), and there is no application scope, so Studio source-control linkage does not apply (sys_app = 0, sys_repo_config = 0).

Biggest gap: nothing detects a hand-edit in the UI before the next scripted rebuild overwrites it. A CI dry-run gate closes that. Detail: docs/CONFIG_TRACKING.md.

Watch one number: Missing category must be 0. It is the only metric that detects a skipped derive pass, and a non-zero value means records are silently absent from the category chart and the map.

widgets.label: Dashboard design summary
widgets.html:
Structure

  • Overview — the working view: at-a-glance counts, two feeds, the map, breakdowns
  • Integration & Health — this tab: sync metrics, design notes, runbook
  • Every widget is generated from specs/dashboard_toronto_events.json

Two rules the layout depends on

  • Absolute windows ignore filters (followFilters: false): Today / Tomorrow / 7 / 30 days keep their own meaning. Filter-driven widgets use true, so the Category / When / Source pills only affect what they should.
  • The canvas layout is a cache. The renderer reads par_dashboard_widget rows, joined to the layout by a shared sys_id. A canvas with layout entries and no matching widget rows renders empty.

Known limits

  • ~2,300 events cannot be mapped: their feed rows carry no coordinates
  • Rebuild with --update; delete-then-create mints a new sys_id and breaks every saved link

widgets.label: Backup and rebuild
widgets.html:
What backs this up

Everything here is generated from a spec by an idempotent script, and all of it lives in github.com/eltonaguiar/ServiceNowDBIntegration (branch main).

Rebuild order

  1. create_table.py — table + columns (specs/u_toronto_event.json)
  2. create_reports.py — the reports (specs/reports_toronto_events.json)
  3. create_dashboard.py — both tabs (specs/dashboard_toronto_events.json)
  4. create_map_source.py — the Geomap mapping chain
  5. backfill_geo_category.py — derived category + venue references
  6. import_events.py — pull the feed

fresh_instance.sh runs that sequence end to end. specs/templates/*.json are load-bearing: they hold the captured native component_props per visualization, and losing them breaks chart rendering.

Update sets do capture most of this automatically — the Default set already holds our schema, reports and PAR dashboard records. What they do not capture: sys_report_map_source, cmn_location rows, and the event data.

GitHub source linkage (sys_repo_config) is for scoped applications; these records are global scope, so it does not apply here.

Full detail: docs/BACKUP.md in that repo.
